feat(turning): threading infeed method and decreasing-depth pass schedule

A Threading op now carries an infeed plan: radial, flank (with a
compound angle) or alternating-flank infeed; constant-depth or
constant-area (first depth x sqrt(n), clamped at a minimum depth per
pass) schedule; a finish allowance; and spring passes at full depth.
The kernel lays the pass list from it (turning::infeed), shifting
each flank pass's start along the lattice by its height above the
root x tan(angle) - same lead, same spindle phase - and the verdict
judges the laid V. A flank angle past the insert's half-angle, a
minimum depth past the first depth, an allowance as deep as the
thread, or too many spring passes are refused by name at Create /
Paste / Edit / retype (thread_gate) and again at Generate.

The default plan reproduces the old ladder exactly: no golden moved,
the stamp digests the plan only when it is not the default, and the
project key is written only when it is not the default (no version
step). The thread-cycle record takes the plan's allowance, spring
passes and flank angle (included, 2x); alternating infeed carries no
record. UI: the Passes tab gains the plan's rows.

Fixes #416

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified

With the G76Cycle post option the control cuts the passes itself, so
the thread-cycle record now states exactly the passes the kernel laid
and the verdict judged, in the cycle's own terms: first depth dd, the
minimum dmin (the rung for constant depth, which the control's clamp
turns into equal steps), the finishing pass's own depth d, m - 1
spring passes, tool angle a = 2 x flank angle, and a flank record
starting at the crest's flank station.

Golden change, on purpose: thread_g76.nc goes from
`G76 P010000 Q400 R0` to `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`. With R0 the control
roughs 0.4, 0.8, 1.2 and then cuts its finishing pass at the root a
second time - a fourth pass at full depth the verdict never judged
(not a gouge, the same root, but not what was verified). R0.4 is the
finishing pass's own depth, so the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and
finishes at 1.2: the three passes verified. The G32 output and the
laid passes are unchanged. (The #363 research read the mismatch as a
decreasing ladder; dmin = infeed already clamped every step to the
rung, so the roughing matched - the extra root pass was the gap.)

Refused by name with G76 chosen: alternating flank infeed (new
`alternating` flag on the record, `ALT 1` in the stream only when set,
an optional project cache key), a flank angle whose double is not a
G76 tool angle, and a one-pass thread. lathe_post_g76_schedule models
the control's schedule from the posted words and pins it equal to
the laid depths and stations (golden thread_g76_area.nc).

Fixes #417

feat(turning): threading option to repeat each roughing depth

A Threading op's infeed plan gains "repeat each depth" (default off):
every roughing pass above the root is followed by an identical copy of
itself - same tip, same lattice shift, same helix phase - before the
ladder steps deeper ("spring at each depth"). The finishing and spring
passes at the root are not repeated; alternating infeed counts depths,
not cuts, so a repeat keeps its flank. The verdict judges the laid
passes, repeats included, and stays clean.

G32 passes only: the thread-cycle record carries a repeat_each_depth
flag (`REP 1` in the stream, property RepeatEachDepth, cache key only
when set) and fanuc-lathe's G76 refuses it by name. Defaults are
byte-identical: no extra stamp byte, no project key, no stream word,
no golden moved. UI: a "Repeat each depth" checkbox on the Passes tab,
its tooltip noting tooling makers recommend against routine spring
passes.

Fixes #418

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(turning): in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain

A Threading op's infeed plan gains chip-break dips (interval, radial
height, length; interval 0 = off, the default). Each roughing pass lifts
radially and returns a few times along the thread, inside its one
synchronized chain: a dip is a variable-radius thread half-turn (same
half lead of axial travel, the radius ramping out or back), so the
station every spindle angle meets - the helix phase - is the plain
pass's. Never deeper than the pass (a radial lift on the pass's own
station stands inside its V), ramps kept under 45 degrees (diameter
change below axial travel), never in the first or last lead, never on
the finishing, spring or repeat passes, height at most every dipped
pass's depth of cut. Refused by name otherwise.

Posting: fanuc-lathe declares continuousThreading = true, citing FANUC
B-64304EN-1 sections 3.4 (continuous threading keeps spindle sync at
block joints) and 3.2 (WARNING 6: a threading block after a threading
block starts without waiting for the one-rotation signal; G32 tapers,
F the Z lead up to 45 degrees), and writes each dip as G32 X Z F,
refusing a segment that does not continue a G32 chain, is steeper than
45 degrees or deeper than its plunge. The record carries
chip_break_dips (DIP 1, ChipBreakDips, cache key only when set); the
section carries PARAM ChipBreakDips, which the engine refuses by name
for a script without the flag; G76 refuses dips by name. The thread
verdict re-reads every chain for the phase, depth, slope and placement
laws and convicts a breach as a gouge (holds the post).

Defaults byte-identical: no stamp byte, project key, stream word or
PARAM; no golden moved. New golden thread_g32_dips.nc. UI: dip rows on
the Passes tab.

Fixes #419

fix(post): the PathPilot G76 reads the finishing step #417 states

Merging main brought #612's Tormach lathe post, which refused any
non-zero FinishAllowance. Under #417 the field is the finishing pass's
own step (never 0 on a laid ladder), so every LinuxCNC G76 was refused.
The post now accepts the step R1's equal ladder takes itself
(K - (ceil(K/J) - 1)*J) and refuses any other, and an alternating
record, by name.

Also: ThreadCycle.alternating in the recorded_streams fixture, and the
infeed pin asserts rest::prior_digest is equal before the save and
after the load (the Stale-after-load seen on another platform is a
main defect: the save snaps moves to the 1 um lattice while the path
signature hashes the unsnapped ones - reported separately).

Refs #417
